Two copper vessels A and B have the same base area but of different shapes. A takes twice the volume of water as that B requires to fill upto a particular common height. Then the correct statement among the following is :
options: Vessel B weighs twice that of A.
Pressure on the base area of vessels A and B is same.
Pressure on the base area of vessels A and B is not same.

explanation: p = ρgh depends only on depth, not vessel shape → same pressure.

question: Water flows in streamline motion through a horizontal pipe of circular cross-section. The pressure difference of water between P and Q is 15 N m⁻². The areas of cross-section at P and Q are 40 cm² and 20 cm² respectively. The rate of flow of water through the pipe (in cm³ s⁻¹) is: (density of water = 1000 kg m⁻³)
explanation: v₂ = 2v₁; Δp = ½ρ(3v₁²) = 15 → v₁ = 0.1 m/s; Q = 40 cm² × 0.1 m/s = 400 cm³/s.

explanation: m = 2πrS/g ∝ r → doubling r doubles m → 10 g.

question: A capillary tube of radius r is immersed in water and water rises in it to height h. The mass of water in the capillary tube is 5 g. Another capillary tube of radius 2r is immersed in water. The mass of water that will rise in this tube is:
explanation: 2π r S cosθ = m g ⇒ mass m ∝ radius r. When radius is doubled (2r), mass of water supported doubles: m' = 2 × 5 g = 10 g. | Hint: Surface tension upward pull 2π r S balances weight mg.
